header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Spend Generously for the Expedition to Tabook

blocks.text:
With great enthusiasm, the wealthy Sahabah (RA) spent in this good cause anticipating the rewards from Allaah. Those Sahabah (RA) who were less wealthy assisted those who were poorer than them. They would even bring their camels to one or two persons, asking them to ride in turns. Some people would even bring some money and give it to someone leaving on the expedition. In fact, even the ladies assisted those in every way they could. Hadhrat Ummu Sinaan Aslamiyya (RA) says that she saw a cloth spread out in front of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) in her room, which was filled with bangles, bracelets, anklets, earrings, rings and other jewellery that the women had sent to assist the Muslim army in its preparations. The Muslims were suffering poverty at that time and because it was a time when the fruit crops were ripe and shady areas were sought after. People therefore preferred to stay at home and disliked leaving.
Rasulullaah ﷺ hastened and intensified preparations and made the army camp at Thaniyyatul Wadaa (just outside Madinah). The army was so large that their names could not be contained in one register. Few were those who intended to absent themselves for they knew that their absence would be unknown only until Allaah reveals some revelation to Rasulullaah ﷺ (a time when they would suffer much embarrassment). When Rasulullaah ﷺ was ready to leave, he appointed Hadhrat Sibaa bin Urfuta Ghifaari (RA) as his deputy in Madinah. According to others, Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed the Sahabah (RA) saying, "Take many pairs of shoes along because as long as a person is wearing shoes, he is like one who is riding." As Rasulullaah ﷺ travelled, Ibn Ubay and other Munaafiqeen drew back saying, "Muhammad wants to fight the Romans despite his arduous condition coupled with the extreme heat and the long journey towards an army he has no power to combat. Does he think that fighting the Romans is child's play?" The Munaafiqeen with Ibn Ubay expressed the same opinions. To make people panic about the safety of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA), he also added, "By Allaah! It is as if I can already see the companions of Muhammad tied up in ropes tomorrow."
When Rasulullaah ﷺ left from Thaniyyatul Wadaa for Tabook, he had already flown the large and small flags. He handed over the biggest flag to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), another large flag to Hadhrat Zubayr (RA), the flag of the Aws tribe to Hadhrat Usayd bin Hudhayr (RA) and the flag of the Khazraj tribe to either Hadhrat Abu Dujaana (RA) or to Hadhrat Hubaab bin Mundhir (RA). In total there were thirty thousand people with Rasulullaah ﷺ including ten thousand horsemen. Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed every tribe of the Ansaar to carry its own large and small flags. The other Arab tribes also carried their large and small flags. [^1]
